subject: Compliance intake & IAM evidence — next steps after demo
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance intake & IAM evidence — next steps after demo

Thanks again for the demo earlier, Alex — great to see how MedSync is thinking about patient workflows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep the procurement/compliance path moving: 

1) Compliance posture: could you confirm the current SOC 2 status (Type II vs Type I, or in-progress) and any recent external pen test or gap remediation notes? Also confirm whether HIPAA applies to the data flows Redwood would see if you host inference in our Dedicated or Private options.

2) Vendor security questionnaire: we'd like to kick off a short VSQ exchange so your security team can validate controls. We can either (a) send our standard vendor intake template (attached), or (b) you can send your questionnaire/portal link — whichever is easier.

3) Identity & Access evidence we typically collect during intake (short list):
   - SSO provider and SAML metadata (entityID, ACS URL, metadata XML)
   - SCIM provisioning: endpoint URL, auth method (bearer cert), attribute mappings
   - RBAC/roles matrix for admin vs viewer vs operator accounts
   - Admin account provisioning and deprovisioning process (owners, SLA)
   - Audit log retention policy for admin actions and access reviews
   - MFA enforcement for admin console and service accounts

I attached a lightweight identity evidence template and a SSO checklist to speed this up. If you can point me to the right security contact (or forward this), we'll open a tracking ticket on our side and estimate a 10-business-day turnaround for the minimal evidence set. Can you confirm target timeline and whether MedSync prefers email attachments or a secure portal?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a HubSpot deal note and a short intake JIRA so we have visibility.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_identity_evidence_template.xlsx (Excel)]
[Attachment: redwood_sso_checklist.pdf (PDF)]

From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@medsynchealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <security@medsynchealth.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Compliance intake & IAM evidence — next steps after demo

Appreciate the clear recap, Ben. Quick answers from our side: 

- SOC 2: We are currently undergoing SOC 2 Type II audit with an expected report in Q3 2026. We can provide a bridge letter and scope statement in the meantime.
- HIPAA: Yes, HIPAA applies — we handle PHI for certain product flows, so we'll need Business Associate Agreement language early in procurement.
- Questionnaire: We host a vendor security portal (https://security.medSynchealth.com/vsq) and prefer that vendors upload templates there, but your attached template is fine if you want to start via email.

Maya is our security lead (cc’d) and will coordinate evidence. She estimates she can pull our SAML metadata and basic RBAC export within 3 business days. I’ve attached the SOC2 bridge letter we have ready.

Maya — can you confirm preferred file formats for SAML/SCIM and whether you need test accounts for validation?

Thanks,
Alex
Director, IT Operations
MedSync Health
[Attachment: medsync_soc2_bridgeletter.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>, Maya Patel <security@medsynchealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance intake & IAM evidence — next steps after demo

Thanks Alex — very helpful. A couple quick coordination items: 

- We'll accept the SOC2 bridge letter to start; we'll request the full report when available.
- For evidence exchange: the templates we attached are fine to upload to your portal. If Maya prefers, we can also create a secure Drive folder and a short checklist to track progress.
- On SAML/SCIM formats: metadata XML for SAML is ideal; for SCIM a secured API endpoint + bearer token is sufficient. If you can provide attribute maps (email, givenName, familyName, roles), that speeds verification.

Next steps (suggested):
  1) Redwood will create a HubSpot deal note (HS-004392) and an internal support ticket (SUP-2134) to track evidence.
  2) Maya to upload SAML metadata + RBAC CSV to either your portal or the shared Drive (link below).
  3) Short intake call with MedSync Security + IT to confirm scope — propose Wed 28 Jul 2026 at 10:00 AM PT. Please confirm or propose alternatives.

Shared folder (redwood side): https://docs.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cExampleDriveId

If that works, we’ll lock the time and I’ll send a calendar invite. Thanks again — my team (cc’d) will be on the call for technical intake.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[HubSpot: HS-004392]
